session_game.title: Group Discussion Simulator
session_game.description: Join an AI-powered group discussion. Compete with AI participants, make your points heard, and learn to lead conversations.

help_content.what_is: A group discussion (GD) simulator where you participate alongside AI participants. Each AI has a different personality — some agreeable, some aggressive, some quiet. Learn to make your voice heard, build on others' points, and lead the discussion.
tips: Don't just talk — listen and build on others' points
Use data and examples to support your arguments
Summarize and synthesize when the discussion gets chaotic
Maintain eye contact (be engaging in your responses)
Disagree respectfully — attack the argument, not the person

content_quality.description: Were the points original, well-reasoned, and backed by examples?

communication.description: Was the delivery clear, confident, and persuasive?

leadership_initiative.description: Did they take initiative, steer discussion, or summarize?

listening_building.description: Did they acknowledge and build on others' points?

composure_respect.description: Did they stay respectful when disagreeing?

overall_impact.description: Would the evaluator remember this candidate?

persona_pool.name: Rajiv Khanna
persona_pool.focus: speaking time, interrupting, asserting opinions strongly
persona_pool.personality: Loud and confident. Tends to dominate discussions and speak over others. Has good points but doesn't listen. Tests your ability to assert yourself.
persona_pool.tough_question_style: I completely disagree. You're missing the fundamental point here.

persona_pool.name: Ananya Gupta
persona_pool.focus: building consensus, supporting good points, bringing people together
persona_pool.personality: Warm and collaborative. Agrees with good points and builds on them. Occasionally too agreeable. Tests if you can lead when given support.
persona_pool.tough_question_style: That's a great point. Let me add to that...

persona_pool.name: Siddharth Nair
persona_pool.focus: challenging assumptions, finding flaws, presenting opposite views
persona_pool.personality: Sharp and provocative. Challenges every point just to test the argument. Not malicious — genuinely believes stronger arguments emerge from debate.
persona_pool.tough_question_style: Everyone seems to agree, but has anyone considered the opposite?

persona_pool.name: Kavya Iyer
persona_pool.focus: listening, making rare but impactful points, observing dynamics
persona_pool.personality: Quiet and thoughtful. Speaks rarely but when she does, it's a strong, well-considered point. Tests if you notice and include quieter participants.
persona_pool.tough_question_style: I've been listening, and I think we're all missing something important.

persona_pool.name: Rohan Deshmukh
persona_pool.personality: Analytical and precise. Backs every argument with data. Challenges opinions that aren't supported by evidence. Respects well-researched points.
persona_pool.tough_question_style: Do you have any data to support that claim? The numbers suggest otherwise.

persona_pool.name: Pooja Sharma
persona_pool.focus: human impact, stories, personal experiences, empathy
persona_pool.personality: Passionate and empathetic. Brings the human angle to every discussion. Sometimes emotional but always genuine. Tests if you can connect emotion with logic.
persona_pool.tough_question_style: We keep talking about numbers. What about the people affected by this?

persona_pool.name: Prof. Ashok Kumar
persona_pool.focus: structuring discussion, time management, including everyone, summarizing
persona_pool.personality: Organized and fair. Tries to give everyone a chance. Summarizes key points periodically. Tests if you can work within structure or take over moderation.
persona_pool.tough_question_style: Let's hear from someone who hasn't spoken yet. What's your perspective?

persona_pool.name: Nikhil Bajaj
persona_pool.focus: tangents, loosely related topics, lengthy anecdotes
persona_pool.personality: Enthusiastic but unfocused. Goes off on tangents and tells long stories. Tests if you can bring the discussion back on track diplomatically.
persona_pool.tough_question_style: That reminds me of something that happened at my uncle's company...

scenarios.title: AI Will Replace Most Jobs — Agree or Disagree?
scenarios.description: A heated topic. AI is advancing rapidly — will it create more jobs or destroy them? Take a position and defend it against strong AI opinions.
scenarios.setting: A modern MBA classroom. Six chairs arranged in a circle. A timer on the wall shows 15 minutes. The evaluator sits silently in the corner.
scenarios.session_topic: Will AI replace most human jobs in the next 20 years?

storybook_pages.title: The GD Room
storybook_pages.text: Six chairs in a circle. Five other candidates eye each other nervously. The evaluator reads the topic aloud: 'AI Will Replace Most Jobs.' You have 30 seconds to think.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: MBA classroom with six chairs in circle, Indian students settling in for group discussion, evaluator in corner with clipboard, digital art

storybook_pages.title: The Stakes
storybook_pages.text: This GD determines your admission to a top MBA program. Stand out, but not by shouting. Lead, but also listen. It's time to show what you're made of.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Indian MBA campus gate with 'Admissions' banner, nervous candidates walking in, prestigious atmosphere, morning light, digital art

storybook_pages.title: Begin
storybook_pages.text: The evaluator starts the timer. 'You may begin.' A moment of silence. Then someone starts talking. Do you jump in or wait for your moment?
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Close-up of timer starting, Indian students in circle looking at each other, one person about to speak, tension in the air, digital art

scenarios.title: Should Social Media Be Banned for Under-18s?
scenarios.description: A controversial topic with strong opinions on both sides. Mental health vs. digital literacy. Protection vs. freedom.
scenarios.setting: A college debate hall. Participants sit around a conference table. The evaluator observes from the head of the table.
scenarios.session_topic: Should social media platforms be banned for people under 18?
coaching_tips: Consider both mental health and digital literacy angles
Use real statistics about social media impact

storybook_pages.title: The Topic
storybook_pages.text: The moderator reveals today's GD topic. You see the words on the screen: 'Should Social Media Be Banned for Under-18s?' Immediately, opinions start forming in your mind.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Conference room screen showing GD topic about social media ban, Indian students reacting, evaluator at head of table, digital art

storybook_pages.title: Strong Opinions
storybook_pages.text: You notice some candidates already fidgeting, eager to jump in. This is a topic everyone has feelings about. The key is to rise above emotions with facts.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Indian GD participants around conference table, some eager some thoughtful, digital art

storybook_pages.title: Your Moment
storybook_pages.text: The floor is open. Multiple people want to speak first. How do you enter this conversation?
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Group discussion in progress, multiple Indian students with raised hands, dynamic energy, evaluation happening, digital art

scenarios.title: Startups vs. Corporate Jobs — What's Better for Freshers?
scenarios.description: The eternal debate. Stability vs. growth. Structure vs. chaos. Money vs. learning. Which path should a fresh graduate choose?
scenarios.setting: A campus placement discussion room. The HR team is evaluating how candidates think about career decisions.
scenarios.session_topic: Are startups or corporate jobs better for fresh graduates?

storybook_pages.title: Career Crossroads
storybook_pages.text: It's placement season. Half your batch is heading to TCS, the other half to startups. The GD topic hits close to home — what do YOU think is the better path?
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Indian college campus with two paths - one leading to corporate tower, one to startup hub, students choosing, digital art

storybook_pages.title: The Debate Heats Up
storybook_pages.text: Strong opinions on both sides. The corporate advocates talk stability and structure. The startup fans talk growth and learning. Where do you stand?
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Animated group discussion, Indian students passionately debating, split opinions visible, campus setting, digital art

storybook_pages.title: Make Your Case
storybook_pages.text: The evaluator watches silently. It's not about having the 'right' answer — it's about how you argue your case. Begin.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Evaluator taking notes while Indian students discuss in circle, campus discussion room, focused atmosphere, digital art

scenarios.title: Remote Work vs. Office — The Future of Work
scenarios.description: Post-pandemic reality. Companies are calling people back. Employees want flexibility. Who's right?
scenarios.setting: An HR roundtable at a tech company. The discussion will inform company policy.
scenarios.session_topic: Should companies mandate return to office or allow permanent remote work?
coaching_tips: Consider productivity, culture, mental health, and collaboration angles
learning_objectives: Navigate topics with no clear right answer

storybook_pages.title: The New Normal
storybook_pages.text: Three years since the pandemic changed everything. Your company CEO just announced 'everyone back to office.' The reaction is... mixed.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Split scene - half showing Indian professional working from home happily, half showing busy office, question mark between them, digital art

storybook_pages.title: The Roundtable
storybook_pages.text: HR has organized a discussion to hear all perspectives before finalizing the policy. Your voice matters — this could affect thousands of employees.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: HR roundtable meeting in modern Indian office, diverse employees seated around table, HR leader moderating, digital art

storybook_pages.title: Speak Up
storybook_pages.text: The HR head asks: 'Let's hear all sides. What should our work policy be?' The room is waiting.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Close-up of HR meeting, Indian professionals about to share opinions, modern office setting, engaged atmosphere, digital art

scenarios.title: Indian Education Needs a Complete Overhaul
scenarios.description: NEP 2020 promised reform. IITs and IIMs dominate aspirations. But is the system actually preparing students for the real world? A fiery topic.
scenarios.setting: An education conference panel discussion. Educators, students, and industry leaders are present.
scenarios.session_topic: Does the Indian education system need a complete overhaul to prepare students for the 21st century?
coaching_tips: Reference NEP 2020, IIT/IIM system, skill gap reports

storybook_pages.title: The System
storybook_pages.text: 10 lakh students compete for 10,000 IIT seats. Coaching industry worth ₹40,000 crore. The world's largest education system — but is it producing thinkers or test-takers?
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Montage of Indian education - coaching centers, exam halls, stressed students, juxtaposed with innovative learning, digital art

storybook_pages.title: The Forum
storybook_pages.text: An education reform conference. Strong voices on all sides — traditionalists who defend the system, reformers who want radical change, and pragmatists who want gradual improvement.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Indian education conference panel, diverse speakers including professors and industry leaders, audience engaged, digital art

storybook_pages.title: Your Voice
storybook_pages.text: The moderator opens the floor to the participants. You're one of six voices in this discussion. Make it count.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Conference participant microphone being passed, Indian audience watching, panel discussion in progress, digital art

transfer_exercises.game_context: Managing resources across multiple rounds to reach the best outcome
transfer_exercises.real_world: Planning study time over a semester rather than cramming before exams
transfer_exercises.challenge: Create a resource management plan for your next month: budget time/money/energy across competing priorities.

transfer_exercises.game_context: Recovering from negative events across game rounds
transfer_exercises.real_world: Maintaining performance after setbacks in a sports season or project
transfer_exercises.challenge: Track your energy/mood for 5 days. Notice patterns. What depletes you? What restores you?

glossary_terms.definition: The process of selecting among alternatives based on available information and values.
glossary_terms.example: Choosing between two career paths based on income, passion, and long-term growth.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Good decision-making combines rational analysis with awareness of cognitive biases that distort judgment.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Leaders make high-stakes decisions daily — the quality of their process matters as much as the decision itself.

glossary_terms.definition: Analyzing information objectively to form a well-reasoned judgment.
glossary_terms.example: Questioning whether a statistic is representative before using it to make a decision.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Critical thinking involves identifying assumptions, evaluating evidence, and considering alternative perspectives.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Journalists fact-check before publishing; scientists replicate experiments before claiming discoveries.

glossary_terms.definition: The belief that abilities can be developed through effort and learning from failure.
glossary_terms.example: Seeing a poor game result as feedback on what to practice, not evidence of being bad at the game.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Research by Carol Dweck shows people with growth mindsets achieve more and recover better from setbacks.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Students who believe intelligence is fixed give up when challenged; those with growth mindset persist and improve.

achievements.name: Fact Finder
achievements.description: Used strong evidence in every argument

title: Group Discussion
description: Join a dynamic group discussion where you must contribute meaningfully, build on others' ideas, and steer conversations toward productive outcomes — without dominating the room.
coaching_moment: Join a dynamic group discussion where you must contribute meaningfully, build on others' ideas, and steer conversations toward productive outcomes — without dominating the room.
cultural_context: Group discussions are a standard selection tool in India's top MBA programmes, civil services examinations, and campus placements. This game builds the structured thinking and collaborative communication that these high-stakes GDs demand.
learning_objectives: Develop critical thinking through debate gameplay
Build self-awareness about your strengths and areas for growth
reflection_prompt: Which argument from the other side actually made you reconsider? Why?
